content: Acid phosphatase is essentially a phosphohomoeasterase enzyme. It is stored within lysosomes and becomes active when these lysosomes fuse with endosomes. The endosomes undergo acidification during their functional processes, which is why acid phosphatase operates optimally at an acidic pH. There are various forms of acid phosphatase present in different organs, and the levels of these enzymes in the serum are utilized as diagnostic markers for diseases associated with the respective organs. For instance, elevated levels of prostatic acid phosphatase in the serum can serve as an indicator of prostate cancer.
